motion.name: route-dim

motion.name: train-run
motion.value: 60 viewBox units/s, 1.4s dwell per station, start 1.8s + 0.35s per line, infinite out-and-back
motion.purpose: A carriage follows the final circular-arc route by distance and tangent, with per-line platform positions at shared capsules. Delayed entrances retain the first stop position. Pausable from the legend, paused off-screen or in a hidden tab, hidden with pulse graphics under reduced motion.

motion.name: station-pulse
motion.value: 1.1s ring, opacity 0.9 to 0, scale 1 to 2.6, ease-out, on the train's timeline
motion.purpose: A ring fires at the arriving train platform on its own route. Parallel lines use separate platform coordinates inside the shared station capsule.

motion.name: theme-change
motion.purpose: Light/dark switch on page chrome; immediate under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
The career is drawn as a rail network. Every build is a line with one saturated color and a letter roundel; every technology is a station; lines cross where skills interchange. The page reads like station signage printed on white enamel: ink-black type in heavy highway-signage weights, square panels, thick ink rules, and nothing that floats. The color comes from the lines, never from the chrome.

Density follows real transit graphics. The home page opens on a full-width octilinear map with the title panel and legend set into its empty regions. Detail pages pick up the same vocabulary through the strip map, the in-train door diagram: a straight run of stops on the line's color. Surfaces are flat. Hierarchy comes from weight, size, and 3px ink borders, not from shadow or tint.

Motion has two authored moments, both on the map. On first load the lines draw along their routes in legend order. Then the network runs: a small carriage on every line travels out and back, dwelling at each station while a ring in the line color pulses outward. The trains are ambient, pausable from the legend, paused while the map is off-screen or the tab is hidden, and absent under reduced motion. Everything else is a state change: hovering or focusing a line dims the rest of the network.
keyCharacteristics: White enamel ground, ink type, six line colors as the only chroma.
Overpass at 800–900 for every title, regular for body, tabular numerals throughout.
Square signage panels with 3px ink borders; circles only for roundels, stops, and interchanges.
Dashed track means "sample", always and only.
A light and a dark theme of the same signage; the route colors never change.

rules.name: The Route Color Rule
rules.body: A line color belongs to one build and is set through `--line`. It strokes, borders, fills spines, and colors underlines. It never sets text color: orange on paper is about 2.5:1.

rules.name: The Monochrome Chrome Rule
rules.body: Masthead, buttons, panels, and headings are ink and paper only. If a non-map element needs color, it borrows the color of the line it belongs to.

rules.name: The Heavy Signage Rule
rules.body: Every title and every interactive label is 700 or heavier: 900 for titles; 800 for buttons, legend names, strip stop names, back links, and text links; 700 for masthead links. Weight carries the hierarchy, and color does not.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: No HTML text drops below 12px. Container-scaled legend text uses `max(12px, ...)` so it holds the floor on short laptop screens. Map labels are SVG and scale with the plate (about 11.7px on the 940px phone plate); the legend repeats every line name as HTML text.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow or kicker text is attached to a heading. The line roundel is the only mark that may lead a title.

rules.name: The Empty Region Rule
rules.body: Panels over the map sit only in regions that have no track or label. Map geometry is laid out around them, never under them.

rules.name: The Flat Enamel Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. When a surface must separate, it gets an ink border or inverts to ink.

rules.name: The Circles Are Stations Rule
rules.body: A round shape always means a stop, an interchange, or a line roundel. UI chrome never gets rounded corners.

dos: **Do** give every build its own line color, letter roundel, and `--line` scope, and carry that color into every element that belongs to it.
**Do** use dashed track (paper dash over the line) and the dashed Sample Tag to mark sample or placeholder content, and say so in words beside it.
**Do** set titles and interactive labels in Overpass at 700–900, and frame panels with 3px ink borders.

**Do** keep authored motion on the map: the draw-on-load and the running trains. Everything else is a hover or focus state transition with the ease-out curve. Trains stay pausable and pause off-screen, and the map is static under reduced motion.
**Do** keep the legend's route explanation in the first viewport at 1280x720 and up.
**Do** dim rather than hide: unfocused lines drop to 12% and unserved stations to 22%.
donts: **Don't** set text in a line color. Line colors stroke, border, and underline only.
**Don't** use dashing as decoration on a real line or panel. Dashed means sample.
**Don't** add shadows, decorative gradients, or rounded corners to chrome. The only gradient is the sample dash, and circles are stations.
**Don't** attach a kicker or eyebrow label to a heading; only the line roundel may lead a title.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or a color outside ink, paper, and the line palette.
**Don't** add scroll-triggered entrances or motion outside the map.
**Don't** route a line through stations it does not serve. The map is a factual diagram; Line S stops only where the site really runs.
